tasks.title: Local ring in HA: event push channel research
tasks.description: Find out whether the HP7 (not the CPD5 already tested) delivers a ring to the LAN so HA can react without the cloud.
tasks.details: Earlier captures showed the CPD5 sends rings cloud-only; the HP7 is a different model and was never captured at a ring. Approach, all passive, with the user's go-ahead: (1) listen to the station's own UDP broadcasts on 50160 multicast 239.255.255.251 and 50162 broadcast while the user rings the bell twice, and see whether the periodic /trans/3.1.1/0/req/8209 message changes or an extra message appears at the ring; (2) a FRITZ!Box capture at a ring to confirm whether the station talks only to the cloud. If a local signal exists, add a passive UDP listener that fires the existing ring event. If not, record that HP7 rings are cloud-only like the CPD5 and keep the cloud ring path. No commands are sent to the device.
tasks.testStrategy: A unit test that the UDP listener fires the ring event on a captured packet; a real ring reproduces it.

tasks.title: Two-way talk: confirm the path and pick the HA approach
tasks.description: Decide how talk can work and whether any part is local. Evidence so far: the EZVIZ talk client is cloud/CAS P2P mediated (VerifyAndTalkStart to a talk server), not a plain LAN channel.
tasks.details: The public EZVIZ Open SDK exposes talk only through its cloud player (startVoiceTalk/stopVoiceTalk, needs an appKey). pyezvizapi 1.0.5/2.0.0 still has no send path. The native talk client connects to a talk server and does ECDH + P2P, which is the cloud relay, so talk is almost certainly NOT purely local on this hardware. Steps: (1) one FRITZ!Box capture while pressing the app talk button to confirm server/port/timing (not content); (2) from that, decide the HA approach. Most realistic: a half-duplex push-to-talk that uploads audio through the EZVIZ cloud API if a documented upload endpoint exists, exposed in HA as a button/service plus a go2rtc/WebRTC mic card. Keep audio OUT separate from the already-working audio IN of the live stream. If no cloud upload endpoint is usable without the appKey SDK, record that talk needs the official SDK and stop.
tasks.testStrategy: Decision written on #15 with the capture evidence; any HA code behind a documented API with a unit test.

tasks.title: pyezvizapi 2.0.0: migration plan (reviewed 2026-11-14)
tasks.description: Reviewed 2.0.0 (PyPI 2026-11-08). HA core still pins 1.0.5.0, ha-ezviz pins <2.0.0. Stay on <1.1 until HA core moves; prepare the migration now.
tasks.details: Findings 2026-11-14. BREAKING for us: (a) flat modules removed: pyezvizapi.camera, api_endpoints, cas, cloud_stream, stream, local_stream (we import all six; new homes: devices.camera, cloud.endpoints, cloud.cas, streaming.cloud.bootstrap, streaming.cloud.protocol, streaming.local.session). pyezvizapi.utils.decrypt_image and pyezvizapi.mqtt stay. (b) Push: legacy HTTP push registration is gone; get_mqtt_client only works after client.enable_channel99() and with a synchronous on_token_updated callback that stores the WHOLE token durably (HA Store, marshalled from the worker thread). The token carries a feature_code marker: our feature_code.py must patch FEATURE_CODE in pyezvizapi.constants, client, cloud.auth, cloud.cas, cloud.token, cloud.operations.* (and set it before login) or the saved token is rejected (EzvizAuthTokenExpired). Monitor MQTTClient.raise_if_failed() and get_push_diagnostics() from the hub health path. (c) Python >=3.12, paho-mqtt>=2, cryptography added as a runtime dependency. WORTH TAKING: register_p2p_session() before the CAS getDevOperationCode lookup (some devices reject the key lookup until the sessionId is registered; could explain CAS key failures on #22-type streams). CAS fixes: ClientType=3 default, framed response reads, expired-cert tolerance. Unlock/lock now raise on application-level rejection instead of reporting success (we should mirror that: check resultCode ourselves on 1.0.5). HPD7 unlock routing (#268): camera wrapper used resourceId instead of resourceIdentifier; we call the client method directly, verify our route string at upgrade. Chime helpers (get/set_device_chime_info, CHIME_INDICATOR_LIGHT=611, SupportChime* flags) match what we already do in device_api.py. Alarm timestamp fix (_shared/alarm_time.py): prefer the UTC epoch over a DST-shifted string; compare with parsing.parse_local_time for the motion sensor. probe_local_stream()/LocalSdkProtocolDetector: detects legacy RTP/PS vs ECDH on a local session, could replace part of our 1 s probe. IDEAS (need the user and the device): LAN RTSP switch (lan rtsp status|enable; hcnetsdk servicesSwitch on port 8000 with the device verification code) - read-only status check on the HP7 monitor first; if the switch exists and enables, go2rtc/Frigate could use plain RTSP. LAN SD-card recording download without the cloud (save clip --source local-playback) and cloud-mediated SD playback (CloudPlaybackClipSource): a local path for the ring clip we now fetch through the cloud. NOT THERE: no talk/voice send path in 2.0.0 (netConfigAndVoiceFileUpload is a file upload, not live talk). Channel-99 is still MQTT after an LBS handshake; it does not deliver rings locally.
tasks.testStrategy: Guard test (tests/test_ha_library_contract.py) extended with the six new import paths; a push test with a fake on_token_updated store; CI green on both HA versions once HA core pins 2.x.
